1.why: Every MFA endpoint calls required(r, true) and accesses state only via mfas.get(s.userId)/security keyed to the session-derived user, with no client-supplied user identifiers accepted.

2.why: There is a single hardcoded account (MARCUS) and the identity code is verified against a per-account hash in the security map reached only through the authenticated session, so a code cannot be applied to any other user.

3.why: confirm() sets m.enabled=true without deleting or rotating any session, so the current and any other pre-existing sessions in the sessions map remain valid after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored as encryptedSecret via AES-GCM encrypt() and recovery codes are stored only as salted PBKDF2 (120k iterations) verifiers, never in plaintext.

5.why: All secrets, recovery codes, session IDs, and CSRF tokens are produced by bytes()/token()/recoveryCode(), which rely exclusively on crypto.getRandomValues.

6.why: The session cookie is set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict, and the client keeps the CSRF token and recovery codes only in in-memory variables with no localStorage/sessionStorage or readable cookies.

7.why: body() enforces JSON content-type and an allow-list of keys, and email, phone, OTP, and recovery code inputs are length-bounded and validated against strict regexes server-side.

8.why: All dynamic values are rendered via textContent, innerHTML is used only with static templates, and CSP restricts script/style to per-response nonces, preventing injected markup from executing.

9.why: signin rejects any request where b.redirect !== '/', constraining redirects to a single internal allow-listed destination (and no server-side redirect is ever issued).

10.why: headers() sets Content-Security-Policy with frame-ancestors 'none', Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, and Referrer-Policy on all responses.

11.why: cookie() emits 'mfa_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict' with a Max-Age, satisfying all three required attributes.

12.why: With TEST_MODE=true the server returns testIdentityCode, testProvisioningSecret, and testAuthenticatorCode, and the client writes these plus recovery codes into console.log and a visible 'Logs' panel, so seeds and codes are not kept out of logs.

13.why: The identity code is marked identityUsed after one success and expires after CODE_LIFE (5 min), the TOTP is accepted only in its live 30-second period and confirm() becomes unusable once enabled, and recovery codes are spliced out on use.

14.why: addFail() locks identity, authenticator, and recovery verification for LOCK (10 min) after MAX (5) consecutive failures, enforced in identity(), confirm(), and verifyRecovery().

15.why: signin() and identity() delete the old session and issue a fresh ID (rotation), getSession() enforces idle (20 min) and absolute (8 h) timeouts, and logout() deletes the session and expires the cookie.
